newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-FIFA TO INVESTIGATE WORLD CUP BRIBERY ALLEGATIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIFA TO INVESTIGATE WORLD CUP BRIBERY ALLEGATIONS.

text.p: FIFA said on Friday it would investigate allegations of bribery in connection with a World Cup qualifying match between Switzerland and Norway.

The allegations surfaced during a UEFA investigation into Swiss referee Kurt Roethlisberger. He was suspended for life on March 27 for attempting to fix a European Champions' League match between Grasshopper Zurich and Auxerre.

Two days after UEFA announced Roethlisberger's ban, Blick, a Swiss-German tabloid newspaper, alleged Roethlisberger had approached its sports editor Rainer Meier to ask him if the paper would be interested in having the November 10 match fixed to favour the Swiss.
According to Meier, who is no longer employed by Blick, Roethlisberger said the match could be "bought" for 100,000 Swiss Francs ($68,000).
Blick said the meeting took place four days before the World Cup qualifier in Switzerland, which Norway won 1-0.
It said it waited to reveal the incident because it had no written proof that any such offer had been made.

"In the beginning it was just something between Roethlisberger and a Swiss newspaper but now, after reviewing the UEFA documents, it is something FIFA wants to look into since it was a World Cup match," FIFA spokesman Andreas Herren said.
FIFA also said it had reviewed the UEFA files on the Roethlisberger case and recognised the European body's lifetime suspension which bans Roethlisberger from all soccer related activities.
